hinge.title: Decide why evaporation can make water, skin, or surroundings feel cooler.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Water vapour condenses into sweat on the skin, and this condensation cools the skin.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Water at the roof's temperature will cool the roof just by wetting it, even if none evaporates.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Sweat evaporates because the skin becomes cooler.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Evaporation cools liquids only; it cannot cool a solid floor or roof.

intelligence.enrichment: Evaporation produces a cooling effect on the remaining water or nearby surface. When water or sweat evaporates from a surface, the surface becomes cooler. The learner correctly applies this rule: Evaporation produces a cooling effect on the remaining water or nearby surface. An earthen pot or fan cools only because the clay or moving air is already cold, not because water evaporates.
